paper.title: Camellia: A 128-Bit Block Cipher Suitable for Multiple Platforms - Design and Analysis (algorithm as specified in RFC 3713)
paper.venue: Selected Areas in Cryptography (SAC) 2000, LNCS 2012; RFC 3713 (April 2004)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm in the paper or specification; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: Camellia with 128-, 192- and 256-bit keys (18 and 24 rounds with FL/FLINV layers, key schedule with Sigma constants, SBOX1 and its derived SBOX2-4), written from RFC 3713, reproduces the 3 RFC 3713 Appendix A vectors
It also reproduces all 3,840 ciphertexts of the authors' (NTT) published test data: 10 keys per key size x 128 single-bit plaintexts, for each of the three key sizes (1,280 per key size)
Decryption (reversed subkey order) returns the plaintext for all 3,843 cases

expected_values_source.what: RFC 3713 Appendix A (3 vectors, SBOX1 table) and the Camellia authors' test data file t_camellia.txt on the NTT Camellia page
expected_values_source.note: the vectors and the S-box are data, copied by script; the single-bit plaintext pattern of the NTT file was verified against the file by the generating script. The program was written from the RFC's description

negative_control: built with -DCAM_SIGMA3=0xC6EF372FE94F82BFULL (one bit of the key-schedule constant Sigma3 changed), 0 of 1,280 vectors match for each key size and the program exits 1
not_checked: the design paper's security claims (differential/linear bounds) and its hardware/software speed figures
keys beyond the 30 in the NTT file and the RFC's 3, and any modes of operation (CBC OIDs of RFC 3713 section 3 are not exercised)
speed (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the 3,843 published Camellia ciphertexts and inverts them. It does not show the security claims hold.
